title: etoro Deepens Its Social Investing Experience with New Options Tools
summary: August 12, 2026 – etoro, the trading and investing platform, is extending its social investing tools to options trading, as growing numbers of self-directed investors explore the asset class. The update lets investors discover active options traders, follow real-time trading activity, and move directly from insight to action within etoro options, while making independent decisions…
body_text: August 12, 2026 – etoro, the trading and investing platform, is extending its social investing tools to options trading, as growing numbers of self-directed investors explore the asset class. The update lets investors discover active options traders, follow real-time trading activity, and move directly from insight to action within etoro options, while making independent decisions based on their own investment objectives and risk tolerance. etoro’s social investing community already helps millions of users learn from one another by sharing ideas, following experienced investors, and building confidence through collective insight. This update brings that same experience to options, giving investors more ways to discover, learn from, and engage with the options community. Bret Kenwell, etoro US Investment Analyst, commented: “As investors grow their comfort with new trading strategies, transparency and community become even more valuable. Seeing how others are navigating the market can spark ideas and highlight strategies investors may not have considered. That said, each investor should always evaluate any idea in the l ight of their own objectives , risk tolerance, and the possibility of loss .” The enhanced experience helps investors find active options traders based on performance, win rate, popularity, and recent activity, then explore public profiles for deeper detail including historical activity, frequently traded securities, portfolio composition, recent positions, and how many other users have duplicated their trades. A live Options Trading Feed shows public trades across the platform, filterable by sector, so investors can see how the community is positioning around specific industries or broader market themes. Selecting “Duplicate”* on another investor’s public position opens a trade ticket with the contract details prefilled, so investors can review, modify, and decide whether to place the trade themselves. Users are also alerted when an investor they follow opens or closes a position, adding context without removing individual control over investment decisions. Kenwell added: “This combines education, market insight, transparency, and community, bringing the collaborative investing experience etoro is known for to a new segment of the market.” The new social capabilities complement the educational and market intelligence tools already available within etoro options, including daily market commentary from etoro analysts, the Academy learning hub, views of the platform’s most-traded underlying assets, and Daily Movers highlighting notable market activity. *Duplicated options trade pricing may differ from the original trader’s price due to market fluctuations. We were founded in 2007 with the vision of a world where everyone can trade and invest in a simple and transparent way. Today we have 40 million registered users from 75 countries. We believe there is power in shared knowledge and that we can become more successful by investing together. So, we’ve created a collaborative investment community designed to provide you with the tools you need to grow your knowledge and wealth. title: Independent Bank President and CEO Brad Kessel Named 2026 West Michigan Business Hall of Fame Laureate
summary: Independent Bank President and CEO Brad Kessel has been named a 2026 West Michigan Business Hall of Fame Laureate by Junior Achievement of the Michigan Great Lakes.
body_text: Independent Bank President and CEO Brad Kessel has been named a 2026 West Michigan Business Hall of Fame Laureate by Junior Achievement of the Michigan Great Lakes. The West Michigan Business Hall of Fame recognizes local business leaders whose leadership and contributions have made a lasting impact on the West Michigan community. Kessel is being honored alongside John D. Loeks, Chairman of Studio C, Celebration Cinema and ShowSpan, Inc. Kessel will be recognized at the 2026 West Michigan Business Hall of Fame event on October 19, 2026, at Frederik Meijer Gardens & Sculpture Park in Grand Rapids. Junior Achievement of the Michigan Great Lakes works to prepare young people for future success by helping students build the knowledge, confidence and skills needed to pursue their goals. Proceeds from the Hall of Fame event support Junior Achievement programs serving area students. For more information about the 2026 West Michigan Business Hall of Fame, please visit Junior Achievement of the Michigan Great Lakes.

title: Amazon OpenSearch Ingestion is now available in GovCloud Regions
summary: Discover more about what's new at AWS with Amazon OpenSearch Ingestion is now available in GovCloud Regions
body_text: Starting today, customers can use Amazon OpenSearch Ingestion in AWS GovCloud (US-East) and AWS GovCloud (US-West), for ingesting data into their Amazon OpenSearch Service managed clusters or serverless collections. Amazon OpenSearch Ingestion is a fully managed data ingestion tier that allows you to ingest and process data before indexing it in Amazon OpenSearch managed clusters or serverless collections. Amazon OpenSearch Ingestion provides a no-code experience to filter, transform, redact, and route data into Amazon OpenSearch Service. Amazon OpenSearch Ingestion automatically provisions and scales the underlying resources to meet the fluctuating demands of your workloads. With this launch, Amazon OpenSearch Ingestion is now generally available in 19 AWS regions: US East (Ohio), US East (N. Virginia), US West (Oregon), US West (N. California), Europe (Ireland), Europe (London), Europe (Frankfurt), Europe (Spain), Europe (Paris), Asia Pacific (Tokyo), Asia Pacific (Sydney), Asia Pacific (Singapore), Asia Pacific (Mumbai), Asia Pacific (Seoul), Canada (Central), South America (Sao Paulo), Europe (Stockholm), GovCloud (US-East) and GovCloud (US-West). To learn more, see the Amazon OpenSearch Ingestion webpage and the Amazon OpenSearch Ingestion Developer Guide .

title: Best AI Help Desk Software for Enterprise in 2026
summary: Compare the best AI help desk software for enterprises in 2026 to automate support, manage tickets, streamline workflows, and scale IT operations.
body_text: Enterprise IT, HR, and operations teams are moving beyond traditional ticketing systems toward AI-native platforms that resolve requests autonomously. The shift is significant: organizations now expect help desk software to deflect routine tickets, route complex issues intelligently, and integrate directly into collaboration tools like Slack. Platforms with Slack-native ticketing capabilities allow teams to turn channels like #it-help into structured intake points without forcing employees to learn new systems. This guide compares platforms using publicly available information about internal-support fit, AI and automation capabilities, enterprise controls, user ratings, and deployment considerations. Product details and ratings should be verified before purchase because they change over time. Organizations increasingly look for tools that handle multiple internal support workflows, not just IT access requests, spanning HR, finance, procurement, and legal teams. Key Takeaways Enterprise AI help desk software in 2026 prioritizes autonomous resolution over simple ticket routing, with documented deployments such as Lemonade reporting approximately 40% automatic resolution across several internal teams using Unthread. Slack-native platforms eliminate context-switching by converting conversations into trackable tickets directly within collaboration tools. Enterprise procurement commonly evaluates SOC 2 Type II, SSO, provisioning controls, auditability, and data-handling policies. HIPAA support and model-hosting flexibility matter when an organization's regulatory or internal AI requirements call for them. Initial deployment can be faster for Slack-first tools, while broad ITSM rollouts involving migration, integrations, governance, and custom workflows commonly require more planning and implementation work. Some AI help desk platforms can identify recurring requests and draft knowledge articles from resolved tickets for human review, reducing part of the manual documentation workload. What Makes AI Help Desk Software Different Traditional help desk systems require manual ticket creation, routing rules, and human triage for every request. AI help desk platforms use large language models to understand request intent, draft accurate responses, and execute multi-step workflows autonomously. The difference matters for internal support teams handling high volumes. When an employee submits a laptop request through Slack, a purpose-built AI agent can check inventory, verify approval chains, and either resolve the request or escalate it with full context attached. Enterprise platforms now support agentic AI capabilities that go beyond chatbots. These systems trigger workflows across integrated tools, update CRMs, provision accounts, and learn from each interaction to improve future responses. 1) Unthread: Best for Slack-native internal support with rapid deployment and proven AI deflection Price: Starting at $50 per agent monthly (5-agent minimum) | Rating: 4.9/5 on G2 Unthread turns any Slack channel into a full internal help desk automatically. The platform achieves 40% automatic ticket resolution across IT, HR, Legal, Procurement, and Finance teams, validated at Lemonade. Unlike platforms that mainly automate access requests, Unthread supports broader internal support workflows with easier admin configuration. Teams can turn a specific channel like #it-help into a structured intake point. Some ticket types remain in-channel while sensitive requests move to DMs or private flows. For HR service desk use cases, employees submit payroll, benefits, or policy questions through private ticketing without leaving Slack. What Sets Unthread Apart Unthread's AI agents triage and resolve requests autonomously, learning from each interaction to improve over time. The self-learning knowledge base drafts articles from resolved tickets, eliminating manual documentation work while keeping content current. The platform integrates with 20+ enterprise tools including Jira, Salesforce, ServiceNow, and Okta. The workflow automations support natural language descriptions, visual builders, or custom code. Key Features Purpose-built AI agents to triage and resolve requests autonomously WebMCP support for connecting compatible external AI agents to Unthread workflows Self-learning knowledge base that drafts articles from resolved tickets Supports rapid setup of an initial Slack-based internal-support channel, with full deployment time depending on integrations and workflow complexity SOC 2 Type II compliant with HIPAA (BAA) on Enterprise plans 2) ServiceNow Rating: 4.4/5 on G2 ServiceNow provides enterprise IT service management, employee workflows, operations management, and cross-department workflow orchestration for complex organizations. The December 2025 Moveworks acquisition enhanced AI capabilities significantly. Now Assist AI handles automation and analytics. Implementation, integration, configuration, and professional services can represent a substantial part of first-year ServiceNow spending, depending on deployment scope and complexity. Primary Focus ServiceNow positions itself for large enterprises requiring workflow orchestration across departments. FedRAMP authorization supports government organizations. The platform unifies ITSM, ITOM, and CSM capabilities. Core Capabilities FedRAMP authorization for government organizations ITSM, ITOM, and CSM in unified platform Advanced workflow orchestration capabilities Custom quote based on products, user counts, deployment scope, and service requirements 3) Freshservice Rating: 4.4/5 on G2 (verify current Freshservice-specific rating and review count) Freshservice provides ITSM and employee service management across IT and business teams. Freshservice includes embedded Freddy AI capabilities across the platform, while the availability and pricing of advanced AI features, copilots, agents, and orchestration capacity vary by plan and contract. AI Agent Studio and expanded agentic service-management capabilities were introduced in 2026. Primary Focus Freshservice positions itself as a unified platform for ITSM, ITAM, ITOM, and enterprise service management, including services for HR, finance, legal, and facilities teams. Core Capabilities Built-in project portfolio management Marketplace with extensive app integrations AI Agent Studio and agentic service-management capabilities 4) Jira Service Management Rating: 4.2/5 on G2 (760+ reviews) Jira Service Management serves thousands of customers with ITIL-aligned workflows and deep Confluence integration. Virtual AI agents are available on Cloud Premium and Enterprise tiers. The platform works particularly well for development and IT teams already embedded in the Atlassian ecosystem. Primary Focus Organizations already using Atlassian products find native integration with Jira Software and Confluence valuable. The platform provides ITIL-aligned service management for IT teams. Core Capabilities Native integration with Jira Software and Confluence Customizable templates for quick setup Incident management capabilities 5) Zendesk Rating: 4.3/5 on G2 (7,100+ reviews) Zendesk offers extensive integrations and AI agents for autonomous ticket resolution. SOC 2 Type II, ISO 27001, and HIPAA compliance make it procurement-ready. The Advanced AI Copilot costs an additional $50 per agent monthly. Primary Focus Large enterprises use Zendesk for deep ecosystem integration needs. The platform offers a large marketplace of integrations and applications. Core Capabilities Omnichannel intake across email, chat, and social AI-powered ticket categorization and routing Support for hundreds of help centers at enterprise scale 6) Salesforce Service Cloud Rating: 4.4/5 on G2 (7,300+ reviews) Salesforce Service Cloud provides Einstein AI for automation and the newer Agentforce AI agents. The platform excels when unified customer records across sales, marketing, and service drive ticket context. Implementation typically takes months and requires Salesforce expertise. FedRAMP authorization supports public sector deployments. Primary Focus Organizations standardized on Salesforce CRM benefit from deep integration with unified customer timelines. The platform offers highly customizable workflows for complex organizations. Core Capabilities Deep CRM integration with unified customer timelines Highly customizable workflows for complex organizations SOC 2, ISO, HIPAA, and FedRAMP compliance options 7) Fin, formerly Intercom Rating: 4.5/5 on G2 (2,900+ reviews) Fin's AI agent provides autonomous resolution capabilities for digital-first companies. The platform supports multilingual teams with dozens of language options. In June 2026, Salesforce announced a definitive agreement to acquire Fin, formerly Intercom, for approximately $3.6 billion , subject to customary closing conditions. Primary Focus Digital-first companies use Fin for AI resolution capabilities. Per-resolution pricing models may increase costs at high volumes. Core Capabilities GPT-based automation for natural conversations Proactive messaging and product tours SSO and HIPAA compliance on Expert tier 8) Moveworks Rating: 4.4/5 on G2 (124 reviews) Moveworks provides agentic AI for multi-step task execution across IT, HR, and finance. The platform supports hundreds of languages and integrates with hundreds of enterprise applications. ServiceNow acquired Moveworks in December 2025, enhancing ITSM integration capabilities. Primary Focus Large enterprises with 10,000+ employees use Moveworks for multilingual AI assistants. The platform handles cross-functional support spanning multiple departments. Core Capabilities Agentic reasoning engine for complex workflows Cross-functional support spanning multiple departments Enterprise-grade security and compliance 9) Zoho Desk Rating: 4.4/5 on G2 (7,551 reviews) Zoho Desk provides an affordable enterprise-capable option with AI features. Zia AI handles sentiment analysis and anomaly detection. The platform integrates deeply with the broader Zoho ecosystem. Primary Focus Budget-conscious enterprises find Zoho Desk accessible while retaining AI capabilities. The platform offers AI included in upper tiers without add-on costs. Core Capabilities AI included in upper tiers without add-on costs Free tier available for initial testing Integration with Zoho CRM and ecosystem 10) monday service Rating: 4.6/5 on G2 monday service brings visual workflow builders and highly customizable ticketing. The platform benefits teams comfortable with the monday.com work management approach. Primary Focus Teams wanting maximum customization flexibility use monday service. The platform provides visual data representation for tracking and strong project management foundations. Core Capabilities Visual data representation for tracking Strong project management foundations Email automation capabilities 11) HappyFox Rating: 4.5/5 on G2 (125+ reviews) HappyFox delivers multi-channel support with AI-powered automation and ticket summaries. The platform includes gamification features for agent motivation. Built specifically for IT service desks with ITIL alignment. Primary Focus IT service desks use HappyFox for ITIL-aligned workflows. The platform supports multi-channel intake including email, chat, phone, and social. Core Capabilities Multi-channel support (email, chat, phone, social) Workflow automation Customizable for various internal support use cases 12) InvGate Service Management Rating: 4.6/5 on G2 (20 reviews) InvGate combines ITSM with IT asset management in one platform. The AI Hub provides productivity assistance while AI Service Agent is available in Pro plans. The platform extends beyond IT to HR, Finance, and Facilities teams. Primary Focus IT teams wanting integrated service and asset management use InvGate. The platform provides combined service desk and asset management capabilities. Core Capabilities Combined service desk and asset management Multi-department ITSM support Free trial available How to Choose the Right Platform Enterprise teams should evaluate AI help desk software based on deployment speed, integration requirements, and the breadth of workflows supported. Platforms that only automate access requests may show high deflection numbers but leave IT, HR, and operations teams handling the same volume of complex requests manually. Consider these factors: Deployment timeline: Slack-native platforms support faster initial setup, while broad ITSM rollouts involving migration, integrations, governance, and custom workflows commonly require more planning and implementation work Integration depth: Check whether critical systems (HRIS, CRM, identity providers) connect natively Admin overhead: Look for visual workflow builders and natural language automation over complex rule engines Compliance requirements: SOC 2 Type II is commonly evaluated; HIPAA with BAAs matters for organizations handling sensitive employee data AI flexibility: WebMCP and model-hosting options prevent vendor lock-in and allow alignment with internal AI policies Why Unthread for Internal Support Teams Unthread delivers the fastest path to AI-powered internal support for teams already using Slack. The platform handles the full spectrum of employee requests across IT, HR, legal, procurement, and finance without forcing teams into rigid ITSM frameworks or months-long implementations. Organizations choose Unthread when deployment speed, Slack-native experience, and proven autonomous resolution matter. The self-learning knowledge base and workflow automations reduce administrative overhead while the platform learns and improves with every interaction. Frequently Asked Questions What is the primary benefit of using AI help desk software in an enterprise setting? AI help desk software autonomously resolves routine requests that previously required human intervention. Documented deployments, such as Lemonade reporting approximately 40% automatic resolution across multiple internal teams using Unthread, demonstrate how AI allows support teams to focus on complex issues requiring expertise. How does an AI help desk differ from a traditional help desk system? Traditional systems require manual ticket creation, routing rules configuration, and human triage. AI help desks use large language models to understand natural language requests, draft contextual responses, and execute multi-step workflows without manual intervention. Can AI help desk software integrate with existing enterprise tools like CRM or HRIS? Yes. Enterprise platforms typically integrate with dozens to hundreds of applications. Look for native connectors to critical systems including identity providers (Okta), project management (Jira), CRM (Salesforce, HubSpot), and HRIS (Workday, Rippling) rather than relying solely on Zapier. What security and compliance standards should organizations look for in an enterprise AI help desk? SOC 2 Type II certification is commonly evaluated in enterprise procurement. Organizations handling sensitive employee data should verify HIPAA compliance with Business Associate Agreements. Additional considerations include SSO support, SCIM sync for user provisioning, and options for dedicated hosting or model-hosting flexibility. How does a self-learning knowledge base improve internal support efficiency? Self-learning knowledge bases analyze resolved tickets to identify repeat questions and automatically draft help articles for team review. This approach eliminates manual documentation creation while ensuring content stays current. The system flags outdated articles when ticket patterns indicate information gaps.

title: E-Way Bill Ship-to GSTIN Error: Causes and Fixes
summary: Learn how to fix E-Way Bill Ship-to GSTIN errors, Bill-to/Ship-to GSTIN mismatch, URP issues and EWB validation errors with examples.
body_text: Ship-to GSTIN errors in e-way bills usually happen when the billing party and delivery party are different, but the ship-to details are entered incorrectly. These errors are common in Bill-to/Ship-to transactions where the invoice is billed to one party and the goods are delivered to another location, branch, project site, warehouse or consignee. For traders, wholesalers, manufacturers and distributors, a wrong Ship-to GSTIN can delay e-way bill generation, create dispatch issues, affect transporter coordination and cause mismatch between invoice, e-invoice and goods movement records. This guide explains the common causes of e-way bill Ship-to GSTIN errors , how to fix Bill-to/Ship-to GSTIN mismatch, when to use URP, and how billing software can reduce repeated EWB validation errors. What Is a Ship-to GSTIN in E-Way Bill? Ship-to GSTIN refers to the GSTIN of the party or location where the goods are physically delivered, wherever GSTIN capture is required in the Bill-to/Ship-to workflow. In a normal transaction, the buyer and delivery location may be the same. But in a Bill-to/Ship-to transaction, the invoice is billed to one party and goods are shipped to another party or location. For example: ABC Traders sells goods to XYZ Pvt. Ltd. XYZ Pvt. Ltd. asks ABC Traders to deliver the goods directly to a project site or third-party consignee. The invoice is billed to XYZ Pvt. Ltd., but the goods are shipped to the project site. In this case, the Bill-to party and Ship-to party are different. The e-way bill should clearly capture the correct delivery details so that the movement of goods matches the actual transaction. For a related e-invoice workflow, read GimBooks’ E-Invoice Bill-to Ship-to Data Entry Checklist. Latest Update on Ship-to GSTIN in E-Way Bill GSTN had proposed enhancements to the e-way bill system around mandatory Ship-to GSTIN capture in Bill-to/Ship-to transactions and voluntary e-way bill closure. The proposed rollout was first moved to 1 August 2026, and later reports stated that these enhancements were kept on hold until further notice after industry feedback. This means businesses should not blindly assume every portal flow has changed permanently. However, the direction is clear: GST systems are moving toward better traceability of billing party, delivery party, GSTIN, URP and actual movement details. For businesses, the right approach is to prepare now by cleaning customer masters, ship-to addresses, URP handling and billing software workflows. Why Ship-to GSTIN Errors Happen Ship-to GSTIN errors happen when the e-way bill data does not properly identify who is billed and where the goods are shipped. Common causes include: Buyer GSTIN copied into Ship-to GSTIN even when goods are delivered elsewhere Ship-to GSTIN left blank where the system expects a value URP not entered for an unregistered consignee Wrong GSTIN entered for the delivery location Registered branch GSTIN not updated in customer master Bill-to and Ship-to address fields mixed up E-invoice data and e-way bill data not matching PIN code and state code mismatch in Ship-to address Wrong transaction type selected Ship-to GSTIN entered in a transaction type where it is not required Bulk upload or API payload passing old customer data A Ship-to GSTIN error is usually not just a GSTIN issue. It is often a customer master, address master, transaction type or dispatch workflow issue. Common E-Way Bill Ship-to GSTIN Error Messages Error / Situation What It Means Where to Check Ship-to GSTIN is missing Required Ship-to GSTIN or URP was not entered Ship-to GSTIN field Invalid Ship-to GSTIN GSTIN format or value is incorrect Ship-to party master Ship-to GSTIN mismatch Ship-to GSTIN does not match the actual delivery party Bill-to/Ship-to details Bill-to/Ship-to GSTIN mismatch Buyer GSTIN and delivery GSTIN are mixed incorrectly Invoice and e-way bill fields URP not accepted due to wrong entry User entered NA, N/A, URD or blank instead of URP Unregistered consignee field Ship-to GSTIN entered in wrong transaction type Ship-to GSTIN passed where it is not applicable Transaction type selection Ship-to PIN/state mismatch Delivery PIN code does not match selected state Ship-to address E-invoice to e-way bill mismatch Ship-to details from IRN and EWB are not aligned E-invoice and e-way bill data If the issue is related to PIN code or state code, use GimBooks’ guide on E-Way Bill PIN Code and Distance Validation Checklist and How to Fix E-Invoice PIN Code and State Code Validation Errors. Bill-to vs Ship-to: Correct Field Mapping Understanding the difference between Bill-to and Ship-to is the first step to fixing Ship-to GSTIN errors. Field Meaning Example Bill-to Party Party to whom the invoice is raised XYZ Pvt. Ltd. Bill-to GSTIN GSTIN of the buyer on invoice 27ABCDE1234F1Z5 Ship-to Party Party/location where goods are delivered XYZ Project Site Ship-to GSTIN GSTIN of delivery party, or URP if unregistered URP or actual GSTIN Ship-to Address Actual delivery address Pune project site Actual To State State where goods physically move Maharashtra A common mistake is entering the Bill-to GSTIN again in the Ship-to GSTIN field even when the goods are delivered to a different unregistered location. This can create a mismatch between invoice records and actual goods movement. When Should You Enter Actual Ship-to GSTIN? Enter the actual Ship-to GSTIN when the party or location receiving goods is registered under GST and has its own GSTIN. Scenario Ship-to GSTIN Entry Delivery to buyer’s registered branch Enter branch GSTIN Delivery to registered third-party consignee Enter consignee GSTIN Delivery to SEZ unit with GSTIN Enter correct SEZ GSTIN Delivery to registered warehouse Enter warehouse/branch GSTIN where applicable Delivery to unregistered site Enter URP where required Delivery to unregistered end customer Enter URP where required Do not use URP when the consignee is registered and has provided a valid GSTIN. When Should You Enter URP in Ship-to GSTIN? URP means Unregistered Person . Enter URP in Ship-to GSTIN when the actual delivery party or consignee is unregistered and does not have a GSTIN. Situation Correct Entry Unregistered consignee URP Unregistered project site URP Unregistered end customer URP Educational trust without GSTIN URP Contractor site without GSTIN URP Registered branch Actual GSTIN Registered third-party consignee Actual GSTIN Do not enter: NA N/A URD Blank value 000000000000000 Buyer GSTIN, unless buyer is also the actual Ship-to party For a detailed guide, read GimBooks’ How to Enter URP in Ship-to GSTIN for Unregistered Consignees. Main Causes of Bill-to Ship-to GSTIN Mismatch Cause Why It Creates Error Fix Buyer GSTIN copied to Ship-to field Physical delivery party is different Enter actual Ship-to GSTIN or URP Ship-to GSTIN blank Required field not filled Add GSTIN or URP Wrong customer branch selected GSTIN belongs to another state/location Select correct branch GSTIN Unregistered consignee not marked as URP System does not know consignee is unregistered Enter URP Ship-to address copied from billing address Delivery address becomes incorrect Add separate shipping address Wrong transaction type Bill-to/Ship-to not selected correctly Select correct transaction type E-invoice data mismatch IRN data and EWB data differ Review source invoice and e-way bill fields Bulk upload error Wrong column or old master data used Correct upload file before generation Most of these errors can be prevented by maintaining separate Bill-to and Ship-to address masters. Step 1: Confirm the Transaction Type Before fixing the GSTIN field, confirm whether the transaction is actually a Bill-to/Ship-to case. Ask: Is the invoice billed to one party? Are the goods delivered to another party or location? Is the delivery address different from the billing address? Is the consignee registered or unregistered? Is the Ship-to GSTIN different from the Bill-to GSTIN? Has the correct transaction type been selected? If the billing and delivery party are the same, the issue may be in normal recipient details rather than Ship-to GSTIN. Step 2: Check Whether the Ship-to Party Is Registered Do not enter URP without checking whether the consignee has GSTIN. Check: Has the buyer provided a separate Ship-to GSTIN? Is the delivery location a registered branch? Is the consignee an unregistered site or end customer? Is the delivery party a contractor or project location? Does the customer have multiple GSTINs across states? If the Ship-to party is registered, enter the correct GSTIN. If the Ship-to party is unregistered, enter URP where required. Step 3: Match Ship-to GSTIN with Delivery Address The Ship-to GSTIN should match the actual delivery location, not just the billing party. Checkpoint What to Verify Ship-to GSTIN Belongs to delivery party Ship-to name Matches delivery consignee Ship-to address Actual delivery location Ship-to PIN code Correct 6-digit PIN Ship-to state Matches delivery state Actual To State Same as physical destination state Distance Based on dispatch and delivery location If the goods are going to Pune, but the Ship-to GSTIN belongs to a Delhi registration, the e-way bill data may create mismatch risk. Step 4: Validate PIN Code and State Code Ship-to GSTIN errors often appear with PIN code or state code validation errors. Even when GSTIN is correct, the address can still fail if the PIN or state is wrong. Check: PIN code is valid PIN code belongs to the selected state State code matches GSTIN state where applicable Actual To State is correct Delivery address is complete Dispatch-from state is correct For a full address validation workflow, refer to GimBooks’ How to Fix E-Invoice PIN Code and State Code Validation Errors. Step 5: Check E-Invoice to E-Way Bill Data Flow Many businesses generate e-way bills from e-invoice data or through the e-way bill by IRN workflow. In these cases, errors can happen when the Ship-to details in the e-invoice data do not match the e-way bill fields. Check whether: Ship-to GSTIN was captured during invoice creation Ship-to address was added separately E-way bill by IRN is using correct delivery details Billing software is overwriting Ship-to GSTIN API payload is passing URP correctly Dispatch team can review Ship-to details before generation For e-invoice-linked logistics workflows, read GimBooks’ E-Invoice Reporting for Export Invoices Within 30 Days if exports are involved, or GimBooks E-Way Bills for e-way bill workflows. Step 6: Fix the Customer and Ship-to Address Master If the same Ship-to GSTIN error appears repeatedly, the root problem is likely in the customer or address master. Update: Master Data Field What to Fix Customer GSTIN Correct buyer GSTIN Customer Branch Correct GSTIN for each branch Ship-to GSTIN Actual GSTIN or URP Ship-to Name Correct consignee name Ship-to Address Complete delivery address Ship-to PIN Code Valid delivery PIN Ship-to State Correct delivery state Transaction Type Bill-to/Ship-to where applicable URP Flag Mark unregistered consignee clearly Status Keep old/incorrect addresses inactive Do not correct only one e-way bill if the master data is wrong. Update the master record so future e-way bills are generated correctly. Step 7: Fix Bulk Upload and API Errors Bulk uploads and API integrations can create Ship-to GSTIN errors even when the front-end screen looks correct. Before bulk upload, check: Upload / API Field Validation Needed Buyer GSTIN Correct Bill-to GSTIN Ship-to GSTIN Actual GSTIN or URP Ship-to Name Correct consignee name Ship-to Address Complete delivery address Ship-to PIN Code Valid PIN Actual To State Code Correct delivery state Transaction Type Correct Bill-to/Ship-to mapping Dispatch From Correct warehouse/location Distance Based on actual route Transporter Details Correct transporter ID/vehicle details If the upload file uses old customer data, the portal may reject the e-way bill even though the invoice appears correct in the billing system. Step 8: Check Whether Ship-to GSTIN Is Required for That Transaction One important point: Ship-to GSTIN should be used only in the correct transaction flow. If it is passed in a transaction type where it is not required, it can create an EWB validation error. For example, if the transaction is Bill-from/Dispatch-from and not Bill-to/Ship-to, adding Ship-to GSTIN may be incorrect. Use this table: Transaction Type Ship-to GSTIN Handling Regular supply to same buyer location Usually not a separate Ship-to GSTIN case Bill-to/Ship-to Enter actual Ship-to GSTIN or URP Bill-from/Dispatch-from Do not pass Ship-to GSTIN unless applicable in system flow Combination transaction Check field mapping carefully E-invoice to EWB by IRN Use the Ship-to details available from invoice/e-invoice data This helps prevent unnecessary validation errors caused by overfilling the wrong field. Practical Fix Table for Ship-to GSTIN Errors Problem Likely Cause Fix Ship-to GSTIN missing Field left blank Enter actual GSTIN or URP Ship-to GSTIN invalid GSTIN entered incorrectly Verify and update correct GSTIN URP not accepted Wrong value entered Enter exactly URP Bill-to GSTIN copied to Ship-to Delivery party is different Enter actual Ship-to GSTIN or URP Ship-to GSTIN belongs to wrong state Wrong customer branch selected Use correct branch GSTIN Ship-to address mismatch Billing address copied into delivery field Add separate delivery address EWB validation error in bulk upload Wrong column mapping Correct upload template Ship-to GSTIN passed in wrong transaction type Incorrect API/billing configuration Check transaction type and payload E-invoice and EWB data mismatch Software overwrote delivery fields Review invoice-to-EWB mapping How Billing Software Can Prevent Ship-to GSTIN Errors Billing software should not leave Ship-to GSTIN entry entirely to manual typing. It should help users select the correct Bill-to and Ship-to details. Useful controls include: Software Control Why It Helps Separate Bill-to and Ship-to fields Avoids billing and delivery confusion Ship-to address master Saves repeat delivery locations URP option Helps users handle unregistered consignees correctly GSTIN validation Prevents invalid GSTIN entry PIN-state validation Reduces address mismatch errors Transaction type selection Applies correct Bill-to/Ship-to logic API payload preview Helps technical teams debug errors Bulk upload validation Prevents repeated file-level mistakes E-way bill status report Tracks pending and failed EWB generation Audit trail Shows who changed ship-to details With GimBooks E-Way Bills , businesses can manage e-way bill workflows more systematically. Businesses can also use GimBooks GST billing software to keep invoice, customer and delivery data organised in one place. Ship-to GSTIN Error Checklist Before Generating E-Way Bill Use this checklist before generating an e-way bill in Bill-to/Ship-to cases: Confirm whether the transaction is Bill-to/Ship-to. Check whether the Ship-to party is registered. Enter actual Ship-to GSTIN if registered. Enter URP if the consignee is unregistered. Do not leave Ship-to GSTIN blank where required. Do not enter NA, URD or dummy GSTIN. Do not copy Bill-to GSTIN unless buyer is also the delivery party. Add complete Ship-to name and address. Validate Ship-to PIN code and state. Check Actual To State. Confirm dispatch-from address. Review transaction type. Check e-invoice-to-e-way bill mapping where applicable. Validate bulk upload or API fields before submission. Save generated e-way bill for reconciliation. How GimBooks Helps Fix E-Way Bill Ship-to GSTIN Errors Ship-to GSTIN errors become common when businesses manage many buyers, delivery locations, dispatch teams, warehouses and transporters manually. GimBooks helps businesses manage GST invoices, e-way bills, delivery documents and customer records in a more organised way. With structured customer and ship-to details, teams can reduce mistakes such as blank Ship-to GSTIN, wrong GSTIN, missing URP, address mismatch and incorrect transaction type selection. GimBooks can help teams: Maintain cleaner customer and address records Use separate Bill-to and Ship-to details Reduce repeated manual entry Track e-way bill generation status Manage GST-ready billing records Improve dispatch and finance coordination For movement-related documents, you can also refer to GimBooks’ Delivery Challan Format and E-Way Bill Format . Conclusion E-way bill Ship-to GSTIN errors usually happen because the billing party, delivery party and actual goods movement are not mapped correctly. The most common causes are blank Ship-to GSTIN, wrong GSTIN, buyer GSTIN copied into Ship-to field, URP not used for unregistered consignees, wrong transaction type, address mismatch and e-invoice-to-e-way bill data mismatch. To fix these errors, businesses should first confirm whether the transaction is Bill-to/Ship-to, check whether the consignee is registered or unregistered, enter the correct Ship-to GSTIN or URP, validate delivery address and PIN code, and update the customer or ship-to master. The best long-term fix is to use structured billing and e-way bill software that separates Bill-to and Ship-to details, validates GSTIN/address data and helps dispatch teams avoid repeated EWB validation errors. FAQs What is Ship-to GSTIN in e-way bill? Ship-to GSTIN is the GSTIN of the party or location where goods are physically delivered, wherever the Bill-to/Ship-to workflow requires it. Why am I getting Ship-to GSTIN error in e-way bill? You may get this error because Ship-to GSTIN is missing, invalid, copied incorrectly from the buyer GSTIN, or not aligned with the actual delivery party or transaction type. What should I enter if the Ship-to consignee is unregistered? Enter URP where the system requires Ship-to GSTIN for an unregistered consignee. Can I enter buyer GSTIN as Ship-to GSTIN? Only if the buyer is also the actual delivery party. If the goods are delivered to a different registered party, use that party’s GSTIN. If the consignee is unregistered, use URP. What is Bill-to Ship-to GSTIN mismatch? It means the GSTIN of the billed party and the GSTIN or delivery details of the shipped-to party are not mapped correctly in the e-way bill data. Can wrong PIN code cause Ship-to GSTIN error? Yes. Wrong PIN code or state code in the Ship-to address can create EWB validation errors even if the GSTIN is correct. Is Ship-to GSTIN mandatory in e-way bill? GSTN had proposed mandatory Ship-to GSTIN capture for Bill-to/Ship-to transactions, but later reports stated the 1 August 2026 rollout was kept on hold until further notice. Businesses should still prepare their master data and software workflows. How can billing software prevent Ship-to GSTIN errors? Billing software can prevent these errors by maintaining separate Bill-to and Ship-to fields, validating GSTIN and PIN codes, allowing URP for unregistered consignees, and checking transaction type before e-way bill generation.

title: 9 Best Juicebox (PeopleGPT) Alternatives for Recruiters in 2026
summary: Weekday is a top Juicebox alternative for recruiters in 2026. Compare AI sourcing tools that go beyond search with built-in email, WhatsApp, and phone outreach.
body_text: Weekday is the top Juicebox (PeopleGPT) alternative for recruiters who want to go beyond candidate search and actually reach candidates through built-in email, WhatsApp, and phone outreach. This guide compares nine platforms that give you sourcing, outreach, and in some cases done-for-you hiring in a single workflow. Juicebox made natural language candidate search mainstream. Type a description, get a ranked shortlist. That is genuinely useful. But sourcing is only half the job. Most recruiting teams hit the wall when they have to pivot from search to outreach, and Juicebox's toolset, while solid on search, leaves multi-channel engagement largely to the recruiter. If you are looking for a platform that finds candidates and moves them toward a conversation without requiring you to stitch together three other tools, this list is for you. Weeday leads this list because it is the only platform that pairs a large verified talent database with fully automated outreach across email, WhatsApp, and phone, and optionally hands the entire hiring motion to a dedicated senior recruiter. The other eight tools on this list each solve real problems for real teams, and we cover them honestly so you can make the right call. Why Recruiters Need More Than a People Search Tool Finding a candidate's name and LinkedIn profile does not get them on your calendar. The real problem in proactive hiring is low response rate, and search depth alone rarely moves the needle. Most candidates worth hiring are passive . They did not apply. They are not refreshing their inbox waiting for your message. Getting a response from them requires persistence, the right channel, and a message that feels personal. Juicebox addresses the search side of this equation well. It does not fully address what comes next: multi-channel follow-ups, phone calls, WhatsApp nudges, and the iterative outreach cadence that turns a cold profile into an interested candidate. Weekday was built specifically to close that gap. Common Gaps Recruiters Hit with Search-Only Tools Single-channel outreach: Most AI sourcing tools send an email and stop. Candidates who do not respond to email often respond to WhatsApp or a phone call. No outreach automation: Recruiters manually copy-paste contact details, draft individual messages, and track replies in a spreadsheet. That process does not scale. No done-for-you option: Small teams with one or two recruiters cannot run a full outbound motion on top of their day-to-day work. A contingency or managed model solves this. Global databases with thin India coverage: Most Western sourcing tools have weak data depth for Indian white-collar professionals, the fastest-growing technical talent pool in the world . These gaps are precisely why Weekday exists. The platform was built by founders who lived this problem while hiring engineers for their own startup, and it is architected to handle everything from candidate discovery through interested candidates landing on your calendar. What to Look for in a Juicebox Alternative The right alternative depends on where Juicebox is failing your team. Here is what separates good sourcing-and-outreach platforms from pure search tools. Weeday checks every box below and adds two capabilities that most competitors in this list do not offer: WhatsApp outreach as a native channel and a fully managed contingency model that removes the recruiter bottleneck entirely. Key Capabilities to Evaluate Database quality and depth: Size matters less than accuracy. A 300M-profile database of verified contacts beats a 1B-profile database full of stale emails. Multi-channel outreach: Email alone is not enough. The best platforms reach candidates on email, phone, and messaging apps like WhatsApp. Outreach automation: AI-drafted messages, sequenced follow-ups, and response tracking should be built in, not bolted on. Engineering and technical focus: If you are hiring engineers, your sourcing tool needs deep signal from GitHub, Stack Overflow, and technical communities, not just LinkedIn. Managed or contingency option: Teams with limited recruiting bandwidth need a partner who runs the hiring motion end to end, not just a tool to add to the stack. Transparent pricing: Hidden pricing and mandatory sales calls add friction. The best tools let you understand cost before committing. Weeday is evaluated against all six criteria below, as are each of the other eight platforms on this list. How Hiring Teams Use Weekday to Source and Reach Candidates Weeday serves hiring teams at seed and Series A startups through enterprises that need to hire technical talent proactively. Here is how they actually use the platform. Copilot Mode (Subscription): In-house recruiting teams with bandwidth use Weekday's database directly. They apply smart filters to find candidates, click to show interest, and Weekday's system emails, WhatsApps, and calls those candidates on their behalf. Responses land in the recruiter's inbox. Autopilot Mode (Contingency): Smaller teams with less bandwidth hand the entire hiring motion to Weekday. A dedicated senior recruiter finds candidates, runs outreach, screens interest, and schedules interviews end to end. The hiring team shows up for interviews. Nothing else. AI Resume Screener (Free): Teams processing inbound applicants use Weekday's free AI Resume Screener to generate a ranked shortlist from their existing pipeline without manual sifting. Engineering Hiring at Scale: Because Weekday's database contains India's largest collection of white-collar professional profiles, including 300M+ verified profiles, it is particularly powerful for engineering hiring in the Indian market. Clients like WarpBuild (YC S21) and Fuze Finance have built engineering teams directly from Weekday sourcing. Multi-Channel Follow-Up Sequences: When candidates do not respond to email, Weekday's outreach system follows up on WhatsApp and by phone. This three-channel cadence is why Weekday achieves a 50%+ response rate on outbound. Pryce Adade-Yebesi of Utopia Labs called Weekday "by far the best tool I've used for sourcing interested and excited candidates." Srijan Shetty of Fuze Finance put it plainly: "Hired our engineering backbone from Weekday." No other tool on this list offers native WhatsApp outreach plus a managed contingency model in the same platform. Competitor Comparison: Juicebox Alternatives for Sourcing and Outreach The table below gives you a quick snapshot of how each platform stacks up on the dimensions that matter most for sourcing and reaching candidates, not just searching for them. Platform Database Size Email Outreach WhatsApp Outreach Phone Outreach Managed/Contingency Option Best For Weekday 300M+ verified profiles Yes (AI-drafted) Yes (native) Yes (native) Yes (White Glove / Autopilot) Engineering hiring, India market, proactive outbound Juicebox (PeopleGPT) 800M+ profiles Yes (email sequences) No Growth plan only No AI-native search, global outreach Gem 800M+ profiles Yes (sequences) No No No Full-cycle recruiting CRM + ATS hireEZ 800M+ profiles Yes (sequences) No No No High-volume outbound, enterprise SeekOut 1B+ profiles Yes No No No Diversity + technical deep search Findem 100K+ data sources Yes No No No Enterprise talent intelligence Fetcher 500M+ profiles Yes (automated) No No Partial (managed sourcing tier) Hands-off automated sourcing AmazingHiring 50+ source aggregation Yes (templates) No No No Tech recruiter, dev communities Loxo 1.2B+ profiles Yes (sequences) No No No Agencies, full-cycle ATS + CRM LinkedIn Recruiter 1.2B+ members InMail only No No No Broad network access Weeday is the only platform in this table that combines verified database access, native WhatsApp outreach, phone outreach, and a fully managed contingency model under one roof. If your bottleneck is getting candidates to respond rather than just finding them, that combination is hard to replicate elsewhere. 9 Best Juicebox (PeopleGPT) Alternatives for Recruiters in 2026 1. Weekday Weeday is a proactive hiring platform built on India's largest database of white-collar professionals, with 300M+ verified profiles and multi-channel automated outreach across email, WhatsApp, and phone. It was founded by Amit Singh, Chetan Dalal, and Anubhav Malik after they experienced the pain of hiring engineers for their own startup. The company went through Y Combinator and is backed by General Catalyst, Kunal Shah, and Amit Singhal. What separates Weekday from every other tool on this list is its answer to the question recruiters actually have: not "can I find this candidate?" but "can I get this candidate to respond?" Weekday's three-channel outreach cadence, email, WhatsApp, and phone, is why it achieves a 50%+ response rate on outbound. Most tools stop at email. Key Features 300M+ Verified Profiles: India's largest database of white-collar professionals, covering approximately 80% of India's technical workforce. Every profile comes with verified contact details , not scraped guesses. Multi-Channel Outreach: AI-drafted messages go out over email, WhatsApp, and phone. Candidates who do not respond on one channel get nudged on another. The system runs without recruiter intervention. Two Distinct Hiring Models: Subscription (Copilot) for in-house teams with recruiting bandwidth, and Contingency (White Glove / Autopilot) for smaller teams who want interested candidates delivered to their calendar without running the outreach themselves. Sourcing and Outreach Offerings Subscription (Copilot): Self-serve access to the database with AI smart filters, plus done-for-you outreach via email, WhatsApp, and phone on candidates you mark as interesting. Contingency (White Glove / Autopilot): A dedicated senior recruiter runs your hiring end to end, from sourcing through scheduling. Success-fee based. Best for teams with less bandwidth. AI Resume Screener: Free inbound screening tool that generates a ranked shortlist from your existing applicant pipeline. Forward Deployed Solutions (RL Environments): Weekday's specialized offering for teams building reinforcement-learning environments. Pricing: Subscription (Copilot): Custom pricing based on outreach credits (typically 10K to 150K credits). Contact Weekday for a quote. Contingency (White Glove): 15% of the hire's annual salary. Free if no hire is made. Includes a 60-day replacement guarantee. AI Resume Screener: Free. Pros Only platform with native WhatsApp and phone outreach built in, not as add-ons. 50%+ outbound response rate, significantly above industry norms. Two models (Copilot and Autopilot) let teams self-select based on bandwidth. Purpose-built for engineering and technical hiring in the Indian market. Approximately 2,000 companies have used Weekday, from seed startups through enterprises. Contingency model is risk-free: you pay only on a successful hire. Free AI Resume Screener available for inbound applicant processing. Cons Database strength is India-centric. Teams hiring exclusively in other markets will find less depth. No free self-serve trial. Outreach campaigns require a paid plan to experience full value. Contingency pricing (15% of salary) is standard for the industry but can feel steep for high-salary senior roles. Weeday is the standard for proactive engineering hiring in the Indian market. Raveesh Motlani of Enterpret called it "the most successful recruitment partner for Enterpret." Vignesh of Openwrench (YC S18) added: "Some of our best engineering hires were brought in by Weekday." If you are hiring technical talent proactively and need candidates to actually respond, start here. 2. Juicebox (PeopleGPT) Juicebox is an AI-native talent sourcing platform built around PeopleGPT, a natural language search engine that lets recruiters describe their ideal candidate in plain English and receive a ranked shortlist. It is one of the most capable pure sourcing tools available in 2026, and its AI Agents can source candidates autonomously in the background. Where Juicebox excels is search. Where it falls short relative to Weekday is outreach depth. Email sequencing is available, but WhatsApp and phone outreach are not native features. Phone numbers are only accessible on the Growth plan and above. There is no managed or contingency model, meaning your recruiting team still has to run the full outreach motion. Key Features PeopleGPT Search: Natural language search across 800M+ profiles from 30+ data sources. No Boolean strings required. Juicebox Agents: AI agents that source candidates autonomously 24/7 based on recruiter feedback, then initiate outreach. Email Outreach Sequences: Multi-step personalized email campaigns with AI-drafted messaging. Sourcing and Outreach Offerings AI-powered natural language candidate search with lookalike profile matching. Personalized multi-step email outreach sequences. 41+ ATS and 21+ CRM integrations for pipeline sync. Pricing: Free plan available. Starter: approximately $119 per month (annual) or $139 per month (monthly). Growth: approximately $179 per month. Phone numbers only available on Growth and above. AI Agent add-on: $199 per month on top of base plan. Pros Best-in-class natural language search across a large, multi-source database. AI Agents run sourcing and initial outreach autonomously in the background. Free tier available for low-volume or trial use. Strong ATS and CRM integration ecosystem (41+ platforms). Cons No WhatsApp or multi-channel outreach beyond email. Phone number access locked to Growth tier and above. No managed or contingency recruiting option. AI Agent is a significant add-on cost on top of an already tiered base price. Limited depth in Indian professional profiles compared to Weekday. 3. Gem Gem is an AI-first all-in-one recruiting platform that brings together ATS, CRM, sourcing, scheduling, and analytics in one connected system. It sources from 800M+ profiles and is particularly strong on pipeline management, email sequencing, and full-funnel analytics. Over 1,200 companies use Gem, including Anthropic, Zillow, and DoorDash. Gem is a strong choice for enterprise and mid-market teams that want a single platform to manage their entire recruiting workflow. Its sourcing product is solid but less specialized than dedicated sourcing tools. Outreach is email-first, with LinkedIn InMail and SMS available on higher plans. WhatsApp and phone outreach are not part of the offering. Key Features Unified Platform: ATS, CRM, sourcing, scheduling, and analytics in one tool. Multi-Channel Sequences: Email, LinkedIn InMail, and SMS outreach with A/B testing and AI personalization. Talent Compass: Pipeline intelligence dashboards with full funnel visibility and source effectiveness tracking. Sourcing and Outreach Offerings AI-powered candidate search across 800M+ profiles. Personalized email and InMail sequences with A/B testing. Candidate rediscovery from existing ATS and CRM database. Pricing: Startups plan: approximately $135 to $270 per month (billed annually) with 500 AI sourcing credits. Professional and Enterprise: custom pricing per recruiter per month. Enterprise deals can reach $95,000+ per year. Free trial available for sourcing and CRM features. Pros The most feature-complete all-in-one platform in this list. Strong pipeline analytics and rediscovery tools. Startup-friendly pricing available for early-stage teams. 4.8/5 rating on G2 from a large reviewer base. Cons No WhatsApp or phone outreach. Sourcing is less specialized than dedicated sourcing tools. Enterprise pricing can be opaque and expensive at scale. No managed or contingency model for teams with limited recruiting bandwidth. 4. hireEZ hireEZ (formerly Hiretual) is an outbound recruiting platform that combines AI-powered sourcing across a large multi-source database with built-in outreach automation. It is purpose-built for high-volume sourcing and offers 700+ medical specialty filters and 290+ programming language filters, making it particularly useful for technical and healthcare recruiting. hireEZ is a solid tool for enterprise teams running high-volume outbound campaigns. Its pricing makes it better suited to organizations with established recruiting budgets. There is no WhatsApp or phone outreach and no managed recruiting option. Key Features Multi-Source Sourcing Engine: Searches LinkedIn, GitHub, Stack Overflow, academic databases, and 50+ other sources simultaneously. Built-In Email Automation: Multi-step email sequences with optimal send-time scheduling, bulk messaging, and LinkedIn InMail integration. Specialized Filters: Over 700 healthcare specialty filters and 290+ programming language filters for technical roles. Sourcing and Outreach Offerings Outbound sourcing across a large multi-source candidate database. Email sequences with personalization, A/B testing, and sourcing funnel metrics. ATS integration with 45+ platforms including Greenhouse, Lever, Workday, and Salesforce. Pricing: Starter: approximately $169 per user per month. Professional: $199+ per user per month. Enterprise: quote-based. Median annual contract is approximately $13,000 per Vendr data. No free tier. Pros Strong high-volume outbound sourcing capability. Highly specialized filters for technical and healthcare roles. Deep ATS integration ecosystem. Useful sourcing funnel analytics for tracking recruiter productivity. Cons No WhatsApp or phone outreach. Pricing is opaque and can escalate quickly for larger teams. Data can lag behind LinkedIn updates, creating occasional stale contact risk. No contingency or managed recruiting model. 5. SeekOut SeekOut is an enterprise talent intelligence platform with a database of 1B+ profiles and advanced filtering for diversity, technical depth, and government security clearance sourcing. It reads GitHub contributions, patents, and academic publications to surface engineering candidates beyond what a standard resume reveals. SeekOut is the right tool for large enterprise talent teams that need deep technical filtering and workforce analytics. Its pricing structure, with contract minimums that can reach $25,000+ per year, makes it a poor fit for smaller teams. Outreach is email only, and there is no managed recruiting option. The company also experienced significant workforce reductions in 2024. Key Features Deep Technical Signal: Reads GitHub, Stack Overflow, patents, and academic publications to infer skills beyond the resume. Diversity Intelligence: Advanced filters for underrepresented talent sourcing. Talent Market Analytics: Workforce planning tools that show where skills are concentrated and how they migrate between companies. Sourcing and Outreach Offerings AI candidate search across a 1B+ profile database with deep technical signal. Email outreach with contact enrichment. Workforce analytics and talent market insights. Pricing: Recruit Core: approximately $149 per month billed annually as an entry point. Enterprise: custom. Median contracts reported between $15,000 and $25,000+ per year per Vendr data. No free tier. Pros Deepest technical signal of any tool on this list, especially for senior engineering roles. Strong diversity and DEI filtering capabilities. Useful for workforce planning, not just individual role sourcing. Cons Enterprise pricing is prohibitive for smaller teams. No WhatsApp, phone outreach, or SMS. No managed or contingency recruiting model. Company experienced workforce reductions in 2024; long-term product stability worth monitoring. 6. Findem Findem is an enterprise talent intelligence platform that uses a proprietary "3D data model" to track how a candidate's skills and career trajectory evolve over time. Instead of keyword matching, Findem searches on attributes, tangible and inferred data points aggregated from 100,000+ sources. It is positioned for mid-to-large enterprise teams that need deep talent analytics alongside sourcing. Findem's attribute-based approach surfaces passive candidates that keyword-matching tools miss. Its pricing, which starts around $8,000 per year and can reach $100,000+, makes it unsuitable for most small or mid-market teams. Outreach is email-based, and there is no managed recruiting option. Key Features 3D Data Model: Tracks skills, career trajectory, and professional attributes over time from 100,000+ data sources. Attribute-Based Search: Searches on multi-dimensional candidate attributes, not just job titles and keywords. Sourcing Copilot and Fia Agent: Natural language search and agentic sourcing with autonomous candidate qualification. Sourcing and Outreach Offerings Attribute-based natural language candidate search. Automated candidate engagement via email. Talent marketing and rediscovery tools for existing pipelines. Pricing: Enterprise-only. No published tiers. Third-party estimates place pricing between $8,000 and $100,000+ per year. No free trial. Demo required. Pros Finds passive candidates that keyword tools miss through deep attribute modeling. Strong workforce planning and talent analytics for enterprise teams. Recent acquisitions (Getro, Glider AI) are expanding its full-cycle capability. Cons Pricing is enterprise-only and opaque. Not accessible for most SMB teams. No WhatsApp or phone outreach. No managed or contingency recruiting option. Inferred attributes are estimates and can vary in accuracy by region and role type. 7. Fetcher Fetcher takes a sourcing-as-a-service approach to recruiting automation. Rather than giving recruiters a search tool, Fetcher's AI continuously finds candidates matching your criteria from a 500M+ profile database, screens them, and delivers vetted prospects to your inbox. It is designed for recruiting teams that want sourcing output without having to run Boolean searches themselves. Fetcher is a reasonable choice for teams that want managed-style sourcing without a full contingency model. Its outreach is email-only, and the platform does not offer WhatsApp or phone channels. Annual sourcing caps on lower-tier plans can constrain high-volume teams. Key Features Continuous AI Sourcing: The platform continuously identifies and screens candidates in the background based on your ideal profile criteria. Automated Email Outreach: Multi-touch email sequences with response tracking and ATS sync. Learning Algorithm: AI improves match quality over time based on recruiter feedback on sourced candidates. Sourcing and Outreach Offerings Automated candidate discovery and screening from a 500M+ profile database. Personalized multi-touch email outreach with response routing to ATS. Diversity filters for building representative pipelines. Pricing: Self-serve sourcing: approximately $149 per user per month. Managed automated sourcing: $499 to $849 per month depending on search volume and role complexity. Pricing: Self-serve sourcing: approximately $149 per user per month. Managed automated sourcing: $499 to $849 per month depending on search volume and role complexity. Enterprise: custom. Median annual contract approximately $11,000 per Vendr data. No free tier or trial. Pros Hands-off sourcing model suits lean recruiting teams without time for manual search. Learning algorithm improves candidate match quality over time. More transparent pricing than most enterprise competitors. Cons No WhatsApp or phone outreach. Annual sourcing caps on lower-tier plans limit high-volume use cases. No true contingency model. Managed tier delivers candidates but does not manage interviews or scheduling. ATS integration and SSO only available on higher-tier plans. 8. AmazingHiring AmazingHiring is a specialized sourcing platform for technical recruiters, aggregating candidate data from 50+ sources including GitHub, Stack Overflow, Kaggle, Behance, Dribbble, and LinkedIn. It is purpose-built for roles like software engineers, data scientists, ML specialists, and UX/UI designers. Recruiters can contact candidates directly from within the platform using email templates and automated follow-ups. AmazingHiring is most useful as a complementary sourcing layer for technical hiring, adding depth and signal beyond LinkedIn. Its coverage for non-technical roles is thinner, and its pricing, between $3,600 and $4,800 per user per year, is significant for a tool that many teams use alongside their existing stack rather than as a replacement. Key Features 50+ Source Aggregation: Profiles aggregated from GitHub, Stack Overflow, Kaggle, social networks, and professional communities. Technical Signal Depth: Reads code contributions, project history, and community activity to infer engineering skills. In-Platform Messaging: Email templates, bulk messaging, automated follow-ups, and outreach analytics from within the platform. Sourcing and Outreach Offerings AI technical candidate search across developer and design communities. Email-based outreach with templates, sequences, and campaign metrics. ATS integration with Greenhouse, Lever, SmartRecruiters, and others. Pricing: Per-seat annual contracts. Estimated $3,600 to $4,800 per user per year. No free tier or trial. Demo required. Pros Best-in-class aggregation of developer and technical community data. Surfaces engineering candidates that LinkedIn searches consistently miss. Useful for niche and senior technical roles where GitHub signal matters. Cons No WhatsApp or phone outreach. Thin coverage for non-technical roles. Price per seat is significant for a tool most teams use as a supplement, not a replacement. Demo-only onboarding with no self-serve trial creates friction for evaluation. 9. Loxo Loxo is an all-in-one talent intelligence platform that combines an ATS, recruiting CRM, AI sourcing, and outreach automation into a single workflow. It targets direct hire recruiters, executive search firms, and staffing agencies that want to manage candidate discovery, pipeline management, client-facing activity, and outreach without switching between multiple tools. Loxo's unified approach is its core selling point. AI sourcing and outreach sit inside the same system as your ATS and CRM, which reduces context-switching and manual data transfer. However, outreach is email-based, phone and WhatsApp are not native, and the AI sourcing quality outside the US market has drawn criticism in user reviews. Key Features 1.2B+ Profile Database: Loxo Source provides access to a large aggregated talent database with contact enrichment. Multi-Channel Outreach Automation: AI-powered campaign-building with email sequences, follow-up automation, and reply tracking. Self-Updating CRM: An AI agent that continuously refreshes candidate records in the CRM to keep contact data current. Sourcing and Outreach Offerings AI candidate sourcing from a 1.2B+ profile database. Multi-step outreach campaigns with AI-drafted messaging. Full ATS and recruiting CRM with client-facing portals for agency teams. Pricing: Free tier: one user with core ATS access. Basic: approximately $109 to $169 per user per month. Professional and Enterprise: custom pricing. AI sourcing and automated outreach are only available on Professional tier and above. Pros Consolidates ATS, CRM, sourcing, and outreach into one platform, reducing tool sprawl. Strong fit for staffing agencies and executive search firms managing client relationships. Free tier available for basic ATS use. Frequent product updates and an intuitive interface praised by users. Cons No WhatsApp or phone outreach. AI sourcing quality outside the US has drawn criticism in user reviews. Pricing for Professional and Enterprise tiers is opaque and requires a sales conversation. AI sourcing and outreach automation sit behind paid tiers, making the free plan less useful for proactive hiring teams. Evaluation Rubric for Juicebox Alternatives Evaluation Criterion Weight What to Test Outreach channel depth 25% Does the platform support email, WhatsApp, and phone natively? Or email only? Database quality for your market 20% How accurate is the data for the geographies and roles you actually hire for? Response rate on outbound 20% Does the vendor publish or demonstrate real response rate data? Engineering and technical depth 15% Does the platform read GitHub, Stack Overflow, and developer communities? Managed or contingency option 10% Can you hand off the hiring motion entirely if your team lacks bandwidth? Pricing transparency 10% Can you understand cost before entering a sales cycle? Weeday scores highest on outreach channel depth (email, WhatsApp, and phone), response rate (50%+ on outbound), engineering and technical focus for the Indian market, and the availability of a true contingency model. Why Weekday Is the Best Juicebox Alternative for Sourcing and Reaching Candidates Weeday was designed to answer a different question than most sourcing tools . Not "can I find this candidate?" but "can I get this candidate interested?" The combination of 300M+ verified profiles, AI-drafted outreach, and a three-channel follow-up cadence across email, WhatsApp, and phone is what produces a 50%+ response rate on outbound. For teams with less bandwidth, Weekday's Contingency model eliminates the tool problem entirely. A dedicated senior recruiter runs your hiring motion from sourcing through scheduling. Weekday was built specifically for the full sourcing-to-response motion, combining a 300M+ verified database with email, WhatsApp, and phone outreach and an optional contingency model.
